text:
Samir Kapoor: Quick follow-up from the modularization RFC — thinking we should shift from "ownership-by-service" to lightweight 'ownership corridors' per capability (routing, cache, session, telemetry). Reason: reduces churn when we split infra for perf.
Maria Chen: Ownership corridors = interesting. Can you sketch what a corridor contains? public iface, SLAs, allowed callers?
Samir Kapoor: Exactly. Minimum: public API contract, recommended call patterns, stability tier (stable/experimental), troubleshooting playbook, and a small set of owners.
Ajay Patel: How would that interact with current repo boundaries? We already have services that cross corridors.
Samir Kapoor: Two approaches: 1) keep current repos, annotate modules with corridor metadata + CI checks; 2) reorganize repos along corridors over time with a migration plan. Prefer 1 for low risk.
Evelyn Park: +1 for gradual. We should also tag tech debt within each corridor so we can prioritize corridor-level paydowns.
Liam O'Neill: For prioritization, propose a debt-bucket metric: impact * frequency * discovery_age. That helps rank what to fix first. e.g., cache-staleness bug: high impact, high frequency, old = high priority.
Maria Chen: Can we run a quick query to estimate frequency from logs? devops-bot, can you surface 30d counts for error codes tied to sessions/caching/routing?
devops-bot: Sure — running queries now. I'll post results as a Gist when ready. :gear:
Ajay Patel: For interfaces, we should define a tiny compatibility matrix: minor changes allowed without rollout, major changes need canary + contract test. Document in corridor README.
Samir Kapoor: Action items: 1) Maria to draft corridor template (API, owners, SLAs, debt list) — due EOD Thu. 2) Liam to prototype debt-bucket calc on last 90d logs — due next Tue. 3) Ajay to add CI label checks for corridor metadata on PRs — start Mon. 4) Evelyn to run intake for quick wins and categorize as patch/medium/large.
Maria Chen: I'll start template. One Q: do corridors map to product capabilities or infra concerns? My vote: mix but favor capability owner first.
Evelyn Park: Agreed — capability-aligned owners reduce cross-team waiting.
Samir Kapoor: Ok let's try this pattern on one pilot corridor: 'session-mesh' (high churn area). If it improves velocity, we'll expand. I'll spin up a 30-min sync invite for Monday to review Maria's template and the devops-bot output.
Ajay Patel: Sounds good. Please add me to the invite. :thumbsup:
Maria Chen: Added notes to the pilot doc in /docs/ownership-corridors (WIP). Link: https://go/internal/ownership-corridors (private).
